text: The repository tracks automated tests next to the code they cover.
why: Untested code has no executable statement of what it must do, so every change is a guess.

text: The repository declares one test command that runs its tests, never a placeholder.
why: Agents and CI run what the repository declares; a missing or placeholder test command makes every run a silent no-op.

enforcement.run: if [ -f package.json ]; then node -e 'const t=(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("package.json","utf8")).scripts||{}).test||"";process.exit(t.trim()===""||/no test specified/.test(t)?1:0)'; elif [ -f go.mod ]; then git ls-files | grep -q '_test\.go$'; elif [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then true; elif [ -f pyproject.toml ] || [ -f setup.cfg ] || [ -f setup.py ] || [ -f tox.ini ] || [ -f pytest.ini ]; then git ls-files | grep -qE '(^|/)(test_[^/]*|[^/]*_test)\.py$'; else grep -qE '^test:' Makefile 2>/dev/null; fi

text: The test command exits non-zero when a test fails: no `|| true`, `; exit 0` or leading `-` masks its status.
why: A test run whose failure exits 0 turns every red tree into a delivered one.

enforcement.run: { [ ! -f package.json ] || node -e 'const s=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("package.json","utf8")).scripts||{};const bad=Object.entries(s).filter(([k,v])=>/^test/.test(k)&&/\|\|\s*(true|:|exit 0)|;\s*exit 0\s*$/.test(String(v)));if(bad.length){console.error("masked: "+bad.map(b=>b[0]).join(", "));process.exit(1)}'; } && { [ ! -f Makefile ] || awk '/^test[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:/{t=1;next} /^[^\t]/{t=0} t&&(/\|\| *(true|:)/||/^\t-/){bad=1} END{exit bad}' Makefile; }

text: Continuous integration runs the tests on every pull request.
why: Only a check on the proposed head proves the merged tree; local green on another tree proves nothing.

enforcement.run: ci=$(cat .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml .gitlab-ci.yml 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$ci" | grep -qE 'pull_request|merge_request' && printf '%s\n' "$ci" | grep -qE '(pytest|tox|nox|unittest|(npm|pnpm|yarn|bun)( run)? test|vitest|jest|node --test|go test|cargo test|make test|uv run|hatch run|poetry run)|uses: *[^ ]*/[^ ]*ci\.ya?ml'

text: The dependency lockfile of the stack is tracked, so every checkout installs the same versions.
why: Without a lockfile a green run on one machine says nothing about the versions the next run installs.

text: No tracked file is a credential file or holds a private key or provider token.
why: A secret in git history leaks to every clone and stays there after the file is deleted.

enforcement.run: ! git ls-files | grep -vE '\.env\.(example|sample|template|dist)$' | grep -qE '(^|/)(\.env(\.[^/]*)?|id_rsa|id_ecdsa|id_ed25519|[^/]*\.pem|[^/]*\.p12|\.netrc|\.git-credentials)$' && ! git grep -qIE -e '-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----' -e 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}' -e 'gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}' -e 'xox[abp]-[0-9A-Za-z-]{20,}'

text: Installed dependencies, caches and bytecode are never tracked.
why: Tracked install output bloats every clone and drifts from the lockfile it should come from.

text: The ignore rules cover the dependency and build directories of the stack.
why: An unignored install directory is one `git add .` away from being committed.

enforcement.run: if [ -f package.json ]; then git check-ignore -q --no-index node_modules/probe; else git check-ignore -q --no-index __pycache__/probe.pyc && { git check-ignore -q --no-index .venv/probe || git check-ignore -q --no-index venv/probe; }; fi

text: A formatter or linter is configured for the stack, so style is checked by a tool, not by review.
why: Style left to review costs a round trip per nit and is applied unevenly.

enforcement.run: for f in biome.json biome.jsonc .eslintrc .eslintrc.* eslint.config.* .prettierrc .prettierrc.* prettier.config.* ruff.toml .ruff.toml .flake8 .pylintrc .golangci.yml .golangci.yaml .golangci.toml rustfmt.toml .rustfmt.toml; do [ -e "$f" ] && exit 0; done; grep -qE '^\[tool\.(ruff|black|flake8|pylint)' pyproject.toml 2>/dev/null || grep -qE '"(@biomejs/biome|eslint|prettier)"' package.json 2>/dev/null || cat .github/workflows/*.y*ml 2>/dev/null | grep -qE 'gofmt|go vet|golangci|cargo fmt|cargo clippy'

text: A TypeScript project compiles with `strict` on.
why: Without strict checks the compiler accepts the null and implicit-any errors it exists to catch.

text: The README states how to run the tests.
why: A newcomer or agent that cannot find the test command ships untested changes.

enforcement.run: cat README* readme* 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE '(pytest|tox|nox|unittest|(npm|pnpm|yarn|bun)( run)? test|vitest|jest|node --test|go test|cargo test|make test|uv run|hatch run|poetry run)'

text: No tracked file holds an unresolved merge conflict marker.
why: A committed conflict marker breaks the build or, in prose and data, silently ships both sides.

text: A repository keeps one instruction file for agents, AGENTS.md; any other agent instruction file is a link to it or points to it.
why: Two instruction files drift apart and agents follow whichever they read first.

enforcement.run: for f in CLAUDE.md GEMINI.md .cursorrules .github/copilot-instructions.md; do [ ! -e "$f" ] || [ "$(readlink "$f")" = AGENTS.md ] || grep -q 'AGENTS.md' "$f" || { echo "$f does not point to AGENTS.md" >&2; exit 1; }; done

text: A fixed defect gets its regression test at the lowest layer that reproduces it.
why: Low-layer tests fail fast and name the broken unit.

text: When a task names an input or output format, at least one test feeds the plainest hand-written example of that format exactly as the task words it.
why: A reader tested only on its own tool's output rejects the short, plain forms real callers send.

text: Every integration or forward is tested against its real receiver or a verbatim capture of the receiver's output, never against a hand-made imitation.
why: An integration is only proven where it is received.

text: Files, functions, tests and work are named by purpose and role, never by phase, ticket, round, date or version.
why: Phase and ticket names lose their meaning as soon as the phase or ticket ends.

text: Every error path has a stated exit code (64 usage, 65 invalid data, 70 internal, 75 temporary) and a message on stderr.
why: Callers and agents branch on exit codes; an unstated one makes a failure look like success or the wrong failure.

text: Values that may hold credentials, multiline ones included, are redacted before they are logged, persisted or forwarded.
why: A secret written to a log or a record leaks to everyone who can read it later.

text: Never change the git stash stack with a bare `git stash` or `git stash pop`; set work aside with a commit.
why: Every worktree of a repository shares one stash stack, so a bare pop can take another lane's edits.

text: Task status lives in valid `tasks/<id>.json` records that only `krn task` changes.
why: Work status travels with the repository, and delivery stays traceable to the task that defined it.

text: The repository contract names a test command, so lanes and the finish gate know what to run.
why: A lane without a test command cannot prove its change and the finish gate cannot refuse a red tree.

text: Agent notes, plans, logs and scratch files go under the git-ignored `.krn/` directory, never into tracked files or the repository root.
why: Agent state is repository-local and must stay out of the tracked project inputs.

text: A session cannot end while the tests related to its change are red: the Claude Code Stop hook runs `krn hook stop`.
why: A gate that lets a session end on an unrun or red test turns a broken tree into a delivered one.

text: A commit that completes a managed task ends with a `Ticket: <id>` trailer; a commit that leaves the task open carries `Refs: <id>` instead.
why: Delivery stays traceable to its task, and the branch that names a ticket must close it before it merges.
